description:
GH: https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/kopitiam/issues/18

`crates/kopi-beans/src/core/tombstone.rs` — `Tombstone::join` guards its two
CRDT preconditions with `debug_assert_eq!` (lines 60-61), and two tests
(`test_join_different_id_panics` @162, `test_join_different_lineage_panics` @170)
are `#[should_panic]` on exactly those messages.

Under `--release` `debug_assert!` compiles out, `join` returns normally, and both
tests fail with "test did not panic as expected". So they are STRUCTURALLY
incapable of passing in release mode — fail every time, clean tree, no defect.
This workspace is release-only (CLAUDE.md Build Rules), so
`cargo test --release -p kopi-beans` can never be green, and a real regression
has to be hand-separated from these two permanent reds. Cannot trust like that.

Options the reporter listed, in rough order:
  1. `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]` on both tests — cheapest, but leaves the
     invariant unchecked in release.
  2. Promote both to real `assert_eq!`. `join` is a CRDT merge — joining two
     tombstones with different ids/lineages is a corruption bug, not a hot path.
     Cost is two comparisons per join.
  3. Make `join` return `Result` and test the error.

Recommendation: (2). A CRDT merge that silently accepts mismatched lineage
produces wrong data quietly, which is worse than a panic. Two `assert_eq!` on a
merge is not a perf problem.

Related (NOT this bead, needs its own): reporter saw `daemon::runtime::*`
(WAL/failpoint/HLC) tests flaky in release — failure count varied 10/11/12 across
repeated runs on an unmodified tree.
title: kopi-beans: two #[should_panic] tests can never pass under --release (rely on debug_assert!)
